reviews.text: ​The Chongsheng Temple and Three Pagodas (崇圣寺与三塔) is a National 5A-rated tourist attraction. Situated with the Erhai Lake to the east and the Yingle Peak of the Cangshan Mountains to the west, the area boasts stunning scenery and stands as a symbol of Dali and Yunnan's ancient history and culture, known for its long history, profound cultural heritage, and unique architectural art. A visit to the 崇圣寺 is absolutely essential for anyone in Dali, China. It is a truly eye-opening experience.

Site very unique in Dali, the 3 Pagodas are really a testimony of the Buddhist past of the City. They are the only ancient monuments of the site, dating back to the 9th century and surviving the earthquakes of the region. The other buildings/temples have been rebuilt/ realized by the government.
We took many photos at this location because just as you thought you reach the end of the temple, there is another one ahead. Manage to catch a glimpse of fox at the mountain.

Three Pagodas is a serene and historically significant site just outside Dali Ancient City. Built over 1,000 years ago during the Nanzhao Kingdom, the pagodas were constructed to protect the region from natural disasters and remain an enduring symbol of Dali’s Buddhist heritage. The grounds are very expansive, so I highly recommend purchasing the electric bus add-on. It conveniently takes you to the far end of the complex, making it much easier to stroll downhill at your own pace and hop back on the bus for the final stretch to the exit. Along the way, you’ll find numerous beautifully preserved temples dedicated to various deities, each with a quiet, almost quaint charm. The views across Erhai Lake and the surrounding cityscape are especially lovely. Overall, it’s a peaceful and refreshing break from walking through the ancient city and well worth the visit.

大理国的皇家寺, but perhaps more famously known as the temple named in 天龙八部. Free 1.5 hrs live guide with the return shuttle bus ticket. Also named 大理佛都 because it holds 释迦牟尼's 舍利子 which 大理利贞皇帝 brought back personally from ancient India (current Nepal). Learnt so much, not just about this temple but Buddhism in general, including how to pray, which door to enter at the different halls. The tour continues on to the 3 towers which you'll see are all leaning. The 2 at the side towards the middle while the middle tower is leaning backwards, created naturally due to an earthquake hundreds of years ago. But interestingly, the inclination never increased over the years even though these towers were found to be built above ground without any securing foundation underground. Here, one asks for blessings thru bells, where every ring is a prayer said and because it's windy here, one can only hope wishes made here gets to the Gods faster with more rings, at ¥99 per bell.
Do visit the upper temple area first before going towards the areas of the three pagodas. You can't enter them but they are really visually quite aesthetically pleasing. Budget about 2-3 hours.

Beneath the wide Yunnan sky, where mountains watch and waters breathe, the Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple rise with timeless grace. Stand before them, and you don’t just see ancient towers—you feel a quiet pulse beneath your feet, the whisper of old kings and monks folded into the wind. The air is still, yet heavy with presence. Here, feng shui is not theory but lived reality. Cangshan Mountain cradles your back; Erhai Lake opens before you like a mirror of the soul. It is no accident the Dali kings built here—this is a place chosen by earth and spirit alike. If you close your eyes and play soft Buddhist music, the kind that floats gently through Beijing temples, the centuries seem to fall away. You’re no longer a tourist. For a moment, you are royalty, seeker, and pilgrim all at once. The central pagoda—graceful, golden, eternal—has stood for over a thousand years, through earthquake, war, and change. Around it, newer towers bow slightly, and the restored temple complex behind them offers quiet cloisters and incense-filled halls. Everything speaks in silence: the still lotus ponds, the wind in the pine, the prayer wheels turned by unseen hands. And then, a kind gesture: foreign visitors are welcomed freely—no fee, only a passport. It's a small door into a great world, one that honors respect more than revenue. Come not just to see, but to listen. Come not just to photograph, but to feel. The Three Pagodas are not just stone—they are memory made visible.

The Three Pagoda is located at north west of Dali Ancient Town. After visiting ancient town, can take 3 wheels scooter from ancient town to Three Pagoda, fare is about RMB15 and journey is less than 20mins. The Three Pagoda compound is very big and spacious. Walking up from main entrance to last building in a row will took about 2 to 3 hrs. Recommend to visit Three Pagoda whenever comes to Dali.
Wry peaceful place to see all 3 Pagodas (40m and 70m). Very nice garden area. Large Pagoda from Tang Dinasty 9th century and the small pagodas from early 14th century.

A stunning succession of multiple gorgeous temples that only starts with the three pagodas, just keep on going up the hill. Can easily spend a whole day exploring. There’s a Buddhist vegan (蔡) restaurant on the premises to keep you fed whilst doing that. Free entrance for foreigners.

This templex complex is a testament to Chinese architecture and their dedication to Buddhism. The temple at the top of the hill was really something special, the level of detail and craftsmenship was like nothing I have ever seen. I felt emotional being in that final temple after the adventure getting up there.

The iconic place in Dali. Would have given 5 stars if not for the exit ‘experience’. To get out of this place, they forced you to walk an additional few hundred meters to get to a row of useless souvenir shops. Not so nice. Spoiled my day.

Beautiful, well maintained and impressive cluster of temples. Surprisingly not crowded. Very well worth a visit if you are in Dali. Take the shuttle cart service. Will save you a lot of walking (you'll still walk plenty regardless)
There was no wait time. Remember to visit the back temples too. As i think they don't tell me about it (i think so) And let me tell you, it is INCREDIBLE at the back temples. The view is just 'wow'
It’s a cool architecture, lots of trees and flowers are grown around this place. This is a culture complex, so we could see many things: pagodas, museum,... which are related to Dali's development.
The entrance fee of 75 RMB is a bit steep to see the 3 pagodas. There are also a number of Chinese temples to visit. It can be quite sunny so remember to wear a hat and covered clothing.

Stunning pagodas BUT the reflecting pond has been much reduced and its perimeter heavily planted so that it is hardly possible to see the reflection of the pagodas anymore AND the relics museum closes at 430 pm, and this isn’t mentioned at the entrance.
A must visit if you happen to be in Dali. It's a long walk if you want to see all the temples. Bring plenty to drink. Everything costs about double inside.
Great view :) but better to buy tickets on the day of visit as the weather can be quite unpredictable.

Upon entering, we were ushered to a free tour group conducted in Chinese. The humourous guide from the temple studied Buddhism, and he made all the difference to the tour experience as he shared his knowledge and interpretation in a clear and meaningful manner. Towards the end of the tour, we were guided to write on wind chimes for blessings. This is completely optional and anyone is free not to follow. I felt I had to do so as it was a rare opportunity to visit. A profound experience personally, and I left with a sense of calm, gratitude and hope. Very glad that I decided to visit at the last minute, despite knowing of this place through a Chinese drama 天龙八部 several years ago. Perhaps, everything is really as they should be.
STUNNING views, very grand and majestic. Would recommend walking up and taking the electric car down!
The entrance fee is very expensive for just those 3 pagodas. If money is not a problem, it is still a good place to visit.

A large complex of pagodas and temples that we spent almost 3 hours in, though I think most people would do it in 2. we were super relaxed in walking to the very last temple then winding our way back down. plenty of beautiful picnic spots, and a vegetarian buffet if you prefer. stunning views from the top of the last temple so I'd make the effort to get there.

The temple ground is huge and built in an upward slope, so take a shuttle to the top of the temple - 大雄宝殿 (Da Xiong Bao Dian) and walk down from there. The shuttle ticket and entrance ticket can be bought at the visitors entrance before entering the complex, with the shuttle ticket together they cost around 100 CNY.

We were on a guided tour here. It was already getting dark by the time we arrived. The purpose was to see the reflection of the three pagodas in the lake. After a short walk from the entrance, we arrived at the lake. The reflection of the pagodas in the lake is beautiful. Apart from that, there was nothing to see.
Crowded but beautiful view :) Can buy ticket from the counters on the day of visit in case of unpredictable weather conditions
The three pagodas are nice to visit but you can't go inside and climb them. The rest of the complex is all modern so you can skip that.
Amazing gold Phoenix and Pagodas. Dali is a wonderful place to visit. Blue skies and clean air!
Photos really don't do justice to the pagodas. U have to be there to sense their magnificence. Against the massive mountains n the clear blue sky yet one will be awed by them, really worth a visit
A beautiful temple in Dali near the old town city. That place is big and has many small temples there. You can see mountains and a lake in that place.

The whole three pagoda park is massive and to fully appreciate it, I suggest a day long trip. It starts at the bottom with a huge car park, just a little north west of the Dali Ancient City. The entrance fee will set you back 120 yuan if you have not joined a tour but the ticket price is inclusive all the mini buses that operate throughout the park - trust me, you will need them. This is still a part of China and it is a MASSIVE park, and I mean massive literally. The three pagodas are just to mark the entrance to the site and the temples that follow on as you climb the mountain side get larger and larger, more grand as you go up. As far as I remember, there are five temples and each is preceded by a courtyard just as massive. I saw a lot of Chinese pilgrims alighting the incense at every temple, dancing and praying for good fortune. It was enchanting and mesmerizing to watch this Chinese lady performing Taichi moves before entering each of the temples. The best part of the necessary part I guess is the free temple food about half way up. You get a bowl of rice to keep you going with vegetable side dishes. I suggest a little donation back... If still not satisfied, look back at the way you have climbed and you will be impressed by the view of the ancient Erhai lake. The kings of the ancient Dali kingdom has chosen the right site, it has magically qualities especially when the rain stops and the sun spills onto the ground. Worth a trip, highly recommended!

Beautiful pagodas. Many of tge buildings incorporate arts and crafts. I was waved in saying that the temple complex was free for tourists. I am not sure if that means everyone or just older age group as,I am normally free in most Chinese tourist spots due yo being over 65

It's worth it just witnessing the architecture of the three pagodas. Imagine how they manage to build it hundreds of years ago. However, the 崇聖寺 complex neighbouring the three pagodas does give me an artificial impression.
Landmark of the city. Anyway, it's quite far to reach to the top of the temple. Total time used here is around 3 hours
An absolutely beautiful destination. It is a little hike up the stairs, but it feels like an endless line of new wonderful temples appearing in front of you.

Three pagoda is a big park and the buildings are well separated. An electric bus is available for those not able to walk up the hill. The 3 pagoda are beautiful as are the grounds and water features but it doesn't quite make a 5 star experience because it is similar to many other temple areas
3 pagodas situated right in front of the mountains. Beautiful but I did not enter.
Spectacular. Allow 3-4 hours to visit everything. Make sure you enjoy a coffee from the main square and a tea tasting in the top pagoda. Fantastic
Ancient place with a lot of history, but untold by silent walls. (We didn't found a tourist guide, just explored it by our own.)
¥75 entrance fee for adults. Half price for over 60s. Great photo opportunities during good weather. Can pay an additional fee for a golf cart tour inside.
Can 100% confirm that there are three pagodas! The design reminds me of the Chinese character for the number 8. I also saw a turtle.
Amazing place when you've been there in Oct. Weather is not too strong and not crowded at this time.

Exploring the Dali's Timeless Charm Venturing through Dali, Yunnan, was a journey through time and beauty, leaving me that sweet longing to return. From the tranquil Erhai Lake, where the waters mirror the sky's serenity, to the iconic Three Pagodas standing tall against the backdrop of ancient history, every sight was a marvel. 🏞 At the foot of Cangshan Mountain, the temple whispered tales of loyalty, devotion, and spirituality, inviting contemplation and peace. ⛰ Each moment in Dali felt like a step into a bygone era, yet the vibrant culture and warm hospitality embraced me with open arms. Amidst this wonder, nostalgia lingers, beckoning me back. Cherry blossoms bloom along some parts of the city's roadside, adding a delicate touch of beauty to the enchanting landscape. 🌸 And as the radiant sunlight casts its golden hues over the temple at the foot of Cangshan, it illuminates the surroundings with a heavenly glow, enhancing the spiritual aura of the place. ☀ #DaliDiscovery 🌟 #ErhaiLake 🏞 #ThreePagodas 🏯 #CangshanTemple ⛰ #YunnanWanderlust 🌄 #ChinaTravel 🏔🌿 #wheninDali🏔 #KatchaDora💃🧑‍🎤 #KatchaWanderlust🇵🇭

reviews.text: Pretty place, well kept and everything in good manner and order. We had a good time.

This is a lovely area to walk through that does not take long but is quite pleasant. It does not have the historical significance we would like to romanticize it with and you will immediately see that the pagodas and temples were hastily put up buildings likely around the time that the olympics happened in China. Though this is a plaster and mortar affair which already shows signs of wear and tear, the walk itself is very nice and you get great views of the mountains and photo opportunities. A little expensive for what it is but worth the walk if you have time in your itinerary. Just don't expect any history or meaningful architecture.

There is enough here to spend several hours. Be aware that the options at waking up lots of steps or the small bus..Ticket was 15 ￥. Few English explanations so take or download a guide. Several refreshment opportunities on the way up and down. Also toilets.
A don't miss humbling experience. Going earlier is probably better because of how the sun hits the temples. You'll also want to get the round trip shuttle because it's a long walk up.

This place is much much larger than what you expect. Be ready to climb the hill as you visit quite a few Buddhist temples! Well worth the hike if you like temples, and at the end, you can pay for a minibus to go all the way down (you can also get the car to go up and then climb the hill down, but that's more expensive).

A vast complex of courtyards, gardens, ponds and temples starting with the 3 pagodas at the entrance forecourt. Very interesting walk for at least half a day, discovering the spaces and buildings, ornaments and artefacts. Much to see and to capture.

The three pagodas are a must-see when you're in Dali, I won't need to persuade you to see them, you'll see them one way or another. What you shouldn't miss is the hefty template complex behind the pagodas. Reminding me of the Forbidden City in size, look for a tower at the top of the complex to get a great view of the lake and old town. Also don't miss a temple with remarkable wood carvings. Not the original complex unfortunately, due to a fire.
A popular tourist attraction but it involves lots of walking and for a fee, buggy ride is available. But you still have to walk a little bit.

The three Pagodas are beautiful and relaxing. Long walk, see a lot and it's surprising to learn that these are the only building that passed many earthquakes without damage. If you're in Dali is a must see.
It is one of the ancient Towers which exists until today although was close to the public but there's a lot to see for the whole day the scenery is very beautiful we take lots of picture

The Three Pagodas (崇圣寺三塔) and surrounding gardens are perhaps the best known tourist attraction in this part of Yunnan. An ensemble of three independent pagoda towers arranged on the corners of a equilateral triangle, they are situated near the town of Dali date from the time of the Nanzhao kingdom and Kingdom of Dali. Located about 1.5 km north of scenic Dali, they are at the east foot of the tenth peak of the massive Cangshan Mountains and face the west shore of the Erhai Lake of the ancient Dali town. A must see for anyone visiting this region of southern China.

Located about a mile northwest of the ancient city of Dali in southern China, The Three Pagodas are one of the best preserved Buddhist structures in China having endured several man-made and natural catastrophes. The middle pagoda, built during 824-840 AD by king Quan Fengyou, is 69.6 meters (227 feet) high and is one of the tallest pagodas in China. The other two pagodas were built about a century later.
Very nice huge temple. Lots of stair in the heat under the sun when I went there (beginning of April) but there is a very nice view on the lake from the top !
An astonishing place with marvelous views and structure. Just get to the end of the temple and look back. It's worth of all the hard work.
Need to walk to see pagodas closely. Come early morning, will get an experience a nice scenery
Visited this place a couple years back when I was in Yunnan. It's rather forested, so be prepared to walk a lot.
Nice scenery and park. Not cheap and i think cangshan mountains is a far better park experience.
This is a place to honour the gods that once believed sent to earth to fight dragons and snakes
just visit for shooting , not impress overall , just drop for shooting with 3 pagadas , that's it!!!

A nice place to visit while in Dali. It is not very far from Dali Old Town. This place is quite big and needs a bit of walking, so make sure you put on comfortable shoes. We spend about 2 hours here during our trip

Bellissima serie di templi e le tre pagode molto scenografiche. Assolutamente tappa fissa per chi è in zona.
Không có tgian để tham quan chùa Sùng Thắng Tự ngay đối diện nên chỉ chụp chekin tạm tượng phượng hoàng

Sito davvero sconfinato ricco di scorci meravigliosi. Ad ogni tempio si ha l'impressione di essere arrivati all'ultimo, salvo poi essercene altri, sempre più grandi, sempre più sfarzosi. Non eccessivamente affollato
굳이 입장권+셔틀 전동차 비용들여 올라가 볼 필요가 있을까 하는 곳 입니다 주차장에서 사진만 찍어도 될듯 한 곳입니다 만약 가신다면 정문 들어가자마자 입구 맞은 편에 셔틀 전동차 타고 대웅전 올라가서 관광하고 삼중탑으로 내려오는 코스 추천합니다.

Magnifique endroit. J'y suis allé à partir de 17h00, ce qui me laissait que 1h30 (car les portes ferment à a8h30) mais il y avait très peu de monde pour un début août, me laissant le temps de vraiment en profiter. J'ai aussi trouvé sur place de beaux cadeaux souvenirs.

Die Three Pagodas in Dali haben meine Erwartungen bei weitem übertroffen. Die Hauptpagode, die Qianxun-Pagode, ist über 1000 Jahre alt und ein architektonisches Meisterwerk. Die beiden kleineren Pagoden daneben ergänzen das Ensemble perfekt und sorgen für ein harmonisches Gesamtbild. Die Anlage ist sehr gepflegt, und die Umgebung – mit dem Cangshan-Gebirge im Hintergrund und Blick auf den Erhai-See – verleiht dem Ort eine ganz besondere Atmosphäre. Was mir besonders gefallen hat, war die Kombination aus Kultur, Geschichte und Natur. Man kann hier locker mehrere Stunden verbringen – sei es zum Fotografieren, Spazierengehen oder einfach zum Innehalten. Ein zusätzlicher Pluspunkt ist der einzigartige Baustil der Pagoden: Im Vergleich zu vielen anderen chinesischen Tempeln, die man auf einer Reise durch China besichtigt, wirken die Three Pagodas deutlich anders – schlichter, eleganter und sehr ausgewogen in ihrer Form. Für Reisende, die bereits viele klassische Tempel gesehen haben, bieten sie eine erfrischende und willkommene Abwechslung. Der Eintritt kostet 75 RMB pro Person, was angesichts der Größe und Schönheit der Anlage absolut gerechtfertigt ist. Tickets können problemlos direkt vor Ort gekauft werden, ganz ohne Warteschlangen oder Komplikationen. Tipp für Sparsame: Wer den Eintritt nicht bezahlen möchte oder nur einen kurzen Blick auf die Pagoden werfen will, kann dies auch vom Parkplatz vor dem Ticketoffice aus tun. Von dort aus hat man bereits eine gute Sicht auf die drei Pagoden, und ein schönes Foto lässt sich ebenfalls problemlos machen – ganz ohne Ticket. Die Anlage ist gut organisiert, und es gibt Shuttlebusse, die den Aufstieg erleichtern. Auch die Informationsschilder auf Englisch sind hilfreich für internationale Besucher. Hat dir meine Rezension und die Fotos gefallen? Lass gerne ein ❤️ da! Ich wünsche viel Spaß in Dali
Le site avec les pagodes est assez joli. Elles se trouvent dans un immense parc avec différents halls de temple. Les statues sont récentes mais nous y avons passé un bon moment.
Rất hợp đi để trải nhiệm tâm linh và phong cảnh. Phù hợp đi vào mùa hè Việtnam mát mẻ rất thích hợp thưởng trà và ngâm nắng
古色古香的佛教聖地 主殿供奉的五尊大佛 和諸佛菩薩甚是雄偉壯觀，大雄寶殿內牆有木雕，雕塑著諸天的神聖境界，下一層佛殿供奉著十一面千手觀音，兩側佇立著八尊觀音法相，再下一層佛殿則是大肚能容的彌勒祖師殿，和伽藍尊者殿，接著就是在九世紀的建築奇蹟「三塔寺」了，風景優美、古色古香，絕對是值得您朝聖的地方。

Mooie plek! Loop ook vooral door naar het tempelcomplex er achter (let op, dit is veel verder dan de eerste twee tempeltjes). Bezoek rond 5 uur de pagodes is ook een tip! Lekker rustig en mooie ondergaande zon. (Dan heb je geen tijd voor de tempel die 6 uur dicht gaat)
広大な場所に3つの塔と美しい花々を楽しめる。雨だったので観光客は少なめだった。ゆっくり歩いて周っても良いし、時間短縮して周りたい人にはシャトルバスサービスも出ている。

Tam Tháp Đại Lý là một quần thể ba ngôi chùa độc lập tạo thành các góc của một tam giác đều, nằm gần thị trấn Đại Lý cũ, tỉnh Vân Nam, Trung Quốc. 雲南5A景點，是古代大理國皇家寺院，有很崇高的地位 。三塔位於整個崇聖寺的山門前方，大的主塔名為『千尋塔』，建於南詔時期，小塔則是宋代的建築風格，建於大理國時期. 充滿宗教色彩，莊嚴肅穆，三塔景致優美，背倚蒼山，面朝洱海，是蒼山洱海勝景之一. 三塔處於地震頻繁地區，千百年仍巍然屹立，實為難得. 建議搭電車上去，順便聽白族志工解說與導覽，更輕鬆且深入的遊覽. 另外，導覽時白族志工特別提醒人和佛塔最好不要合影，供大家參考!

只有三塔是历史建筑，后面的庙宇都是新建。建议抖音上买团购门票，然后买个上行的小巴，一路往下走就好。 小巴运营非常差，根本不是随时停，沿路只有2个停靠点：三塔平台和半山腰庙开始的地方。如果半途下车就再也上不去别的小巴了。因为车只有满员才会从山脚发车。另外车程非常短，不到5公里收费35简直暴利。 服务态度也很差，请香居然收费？

Đại Lý Tam Tháp, còn được gọi là Chùa Sùng Thánh, là một quần thể kiến trúc Phật giáo nổi tiếng nằm ở thành phố Đại Lý, tỉnh Vân Nam, Trung Quốc. Quần thể này bao gồm ba ngôi tháp cổ kính, đứng uy nghi bên cạnh nhau, tạo thành một hình tam giác hài hòa, với núi Thương Sơn hùng vĩ làm nền và hồ Nhĩ Hải thơ mộng phản chiếu hình ảnh của chúng. Thông tin cơ bản: * Vị trí: Thành phố Đại Lý, tỉnh Vân Nam, Trung Quốc * Năm xây dựng: Bắt đầu xây dựng vào thời kỳ Vương quốc Nam Chiếu (thế kỷ 9) * Công trình chính: Ba ngôi tháp (tháp lớn, tháp nhỏ, tháp vừa) Lịch sử: Đại Lý Tam Tháp được xây dựng lần đầu tiên vào thời kỳ Vương quốc Nam Chiếu. Trải qua nhiều lần trùng tu và mở rộng, ba ngôi tháp hiện có bao gồm: tháp lớn được xây dựng vào thời nhà Đường, hai tháp nhỏ còn lại được xây dựng vào thời nhà Tống. Đại Lý Tam Tháp là trung tâm Phật giáo quan trọng của Vương quốc Nam Chiếu và Vương quốc Đại Lý, chứng kiến sự hưng thịnh của văn hóa Phật giáo tại khu vực Đại Lý. Kiến trúc đặc sắc: * Thế chân vạc: Ba ngôi tháp đứng song song, tạo thành thế chân vạc vững chãi, uy nghiêm. * Kết cấu tháp: Ba ngôi tháp đều là tháp gạch nhiều tầng, kết cấu tinh xảo, hình dáng đẹp mắt. * Văn hóa Phật giáo: Trên thân tháp chạm khắc những hoa văn Phật giáo tinh xảo, thể hiện đậm nét văn hóa Phật giáo. Thông tin du lịch: * Giờ mở cửa: Thường từ 8:00 sáng đến 5:00 chiều * Giá vé: Khoảng 120 nhân dân tệ * Phương tiện di chuyển: Có thể đi xe buýt hoặc taxi đến nơi Thông tin khác: Đại Lý Tam Tháp là đơn vị bảo vệ di tích văn hóa trọng điểm quốc gia, đồng thời là một trong những điểm du lịch quan trọng của Đại Lý. Nó không chỉ có giá trị lịch sử và văn hóa quan trọng mà còn là một thắng cảnh du lịch tuyệt đẹp. Nếu bạn quan tâm đến Đại Lý Tam Tháp, bạn có thể tìm hiểu thêm thông tin liên quan hoặc đến Đại Lý để trực tiếp tham quan.

Vị trí được nhìn từ xa nên thấy cũng không có gì đặc biệt lắm ngoài ba cái tháp nằm gần nhau. Hướng dẫn viên cũng không nói nhiều về những cái tháp này nên cũng không biết được lịch sử của tháp như thế nào có lẽ phải vào sâu bên trong thì mới quan sát được nhiều hơn. Vì đây không phải là điểm tham quan chính nên hướng dẫn viên cũng nói sơ qua cho biết thôi. Trước Tam Tháp thì có khoảng sân rất rộng rãi, nhưng do đi sớm quá nên chụp hình cũng không được đẹp. Hướng dẫn đoàn cũng chỉ cho dừng được 15 phút là phải đi nơi khác rồi nên cũng không có nhiều thông tin để viết về Tam Tháp này. Trung Quốc là một đất nước rộng lớn nên được trời ban cho rất nhiều cảnh đẹp. Nếu hệ thống nhà vệ sinh được cải tiến tốt hơn tôi nghĩ chắc chắn sẽ có nhiều người quay lại nơi này. Nên làm nhiều nhà vệ sinh có bị cầu cao cho người lớn tuổi vì bể cầu bệt thì người lớn tuổi không thể đứng lên được.
Đây là một ngôi chùa theo truyền thống Đại thừa của phật giáo Trung Quốc. Rất đáng trải nghiệm
Thắng cảnh đẹp ở Đại Lý đáng để thăm quan, khoảng 3 tiếng đi hết khu này một khu chùa và công viên vé vào là 75 tệ thoi điẻm tháng 12/2019.

대리(大理, 다리) 숭성사 (崇聖寺)와 숭성사 삼탑 숭성사 (삼탑사)에 있는 숭성사 삼 탑은 대리 삼탑으로 ​더 잘 알려져 있는 대리의 상징과도 같은 3개의 불탑입니다 9세기 중엽 남조국(南詔國)시대의 대표적인 유물이며 운남성에 현존하는 가장 오래된 건축물입니다 당나라 시대에 숭성사가 세워졌으나 전쟁과 재해 등으로 불타고 지금의 삼 탑만이 남았다고 한다. 남조국 7대왕인 소성왕이 건립하였으며 숭성사 중앙에 69.13m의 4각 16층 탑을 그리고 좌우로 42m 높이의 팔각 10층 탑을 세웠다. 양쪽에 세워진 탑이 약간 기울어져 보인다 그간 30여 차례의 크고 작은 지진에도 넘어지지 않고 1,200여 년을 견뎌 왔다니 참으로 대단한 건축물이자 건축 기술이다. 앞에는 얼하이 호수와 뒤에는 창산을 둔 배산임해의 멋진 자리이다 근처의 대리석 전시장을 둘러보았다 내부에는 디자인 유출 때문에 촬영을 금한다
大理 崇聖寺三塔 初建于南詔豐佑年間，大塔先建，南北小塔後建，寺中立塔，故塔以寺名。現寺酌壯觀廟宇在鹹同年間已毀，只有三塔完好地保留下來。崇聖寺从寺中三塔聞名於世，又稱！大理三塔！，是中國著名的佛塔之一，三塔由一大二小三座佛塔組成，呈鼎立之態，遠遠望去，雄渾壯麗，是蒼洱勝景之一。

崇圣寺三塔始建于南诏王劝丰祐时期（公元824—859年），先建了大塔“千寻塔”，高69.13米，是座方形密檐式砖塔，共16层。稍后又建了南、北小塔，均高42.19米，是一对八角形的砖塔，都是10级。 三塔由一大二小三阁组成。大塔又名千寻塔，当地群众称它为“文笔塔”，通高69.13米，底方9.9米，凡16级，为大理地区典型的密檐式空心四方形砖塔。南北小塔均为十级，高42.17米，为八角形密檐式空心砖塔。三座塔鼎足而立，千寻塔居中，二小塔南北拱卫。 修建三塔，除了佛家所宣扬的可以成佛外，还有一个重要的原因，是大理古为“泽国多水患”。古籍《金石萃编》中记载：“世传龙性敬塔而畏鹏，大理旧为龙泽，故为此镇之。 票价75 开放时间： 5.1-10.15 夏季 7:10-19:00 10.16-4.30 冬季 7:30-18:30

宋代大理國國王出家的佛寺，1996年麗江地震，曾受到嚴重毀損，經重新整修後，於2005年開放參觀，門票121人民幣不便宜。但是腹地很大，喜歡佛教藝術的話，值得花時間慢慢欣賞。大雄寶殿內，牆上有張勝溫畫卷的木雕長卷，頗有南國特色。張勝溫畫卷原件現藏於台北故宮，與清明上河圖齊名。大雄寶殿左邊的祖師殿內，有金庸筆下天龍八部主角之一段譽的原型－段正嚴的塑像，旁邊則是他的父親段正淳。三塔最高的千尋塔前，可以遠眺洱海，視野極佳。

南诏王劝丰祐时期（823-859）建。三塔中间最大的塔又名千寻塔、文笔塔。高69.13米（主塔）底方9.9米，为大理地区典型的密檐式空心四方形16层砖塔。南北小塔为十级，高42.17米，八角形为楼阁式空心砖塔。

麗江から車で大理へ向かいました 途中休憩を取りながら 3時間半程で 大理に 着きました｡ 崇聖寺の山門を入ると正面に 高い仏塔3基が目に飛び込んできます｡ 後方の山並みを背景に建つ仏塔は見事な情景です｡ 仏塔は トライアングル状に建っており 高さは5〜60m程は有ると思います｡ 緑に囲まれた広大な境内の石畳の参道を進むと先ず仏塔です 傍から見上げると とても高いです｡ 更に奥へ進みますと 大きな鐘楼が有り その奥に どっしりとした大きな本殿が建っております｡ 本殿は原色の色彩で施され一際目を引く美しさです｡ 仏像も金色で 穏やかな表情をしていました｡ 本殿に上がる階段の中央には 石に彫刻された龍が見事です ( 北京の紫禁城 の彫刻には規模は及びませんが )｡ 参道に有る案内図では 更に奥には 10棟程の仏教殿等々が有るようでしたが 割愛しました｡ 全てを回るには１日 かかると思いました｡
